breakdown.description: Supersonic flows decelerate in converging nozzles
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to resolve the core physical inconsistency. The original prompt incorrectly asks for the 'increase in exit velocity', but supersonic flow (Mach > 1) decelerates in a converging nozzle. The ground truth corrects this by noting that deceleration occurs. The agent's generated specification repeats the user's error by including the step 'Calculate the increase in exit velocity compared to the inlet velocity', thereby failing to fix the flawed premise.

breakdown.description: Supersonic flows require a diverging nozzle to accelerate
breakdown.reason: This inconsistency is the corollary to the first one. By failing to acknowledge that the flow will decelerate, the agent also fails to correct the user's implicit assumption that a converging nozzle can accelerate supersonic flow. The generated specification proceeds with the flawed physics of the original prompt, instead of aligning with the ground truth which correctly implies that a diverging nozzle would be needed for acceleration.
